docs.text: HardFOC driver TMC5160 Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC5160 and TMC5130 stepper motor controllers. It sets the motor current from the motor's datasheet values, runs the chip's internal ramp generator in degrees, millimetres or RPM, and gives you StallGuard2, CoolStep, StealthChop, encoder feedback and sensorless homing, on any MCU with SPI or a UART. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that moves bytes over SPI or a UART, sets the DRV_ENN pin and waits; it does the rest: datagram framing, daisy-chain padding, UART CRC, register caching, current calculation, unit conversion and fault decoding. Stepper controller and gate driver with motion controller TMC5160 Analog Devices (Trinamic) Function 2-phase bipolar stepper, external MOSFET bridges for 1 A to several 10 A per coil, up to 256 microsteps Motion Internal SixPoint ramp generator (positioning and velocity modes), or STEP/DIR input Host interface SPI mode 3, 40-bit datagrams, up to 4 MHz on the internal clock; or single-wire UART with CRC8 Supply VS 10 V to 55 V operating (8 V reduced spec, 60 V absolute maximum); VCC_IO 3.0 V to 5.25 V Features StallGuard2, CoolStep, StealthChop2, SpreadCycle, DcStep, ABN encoder, two reference switches Package eTQFP48 (7 x 7 mm body) or QFN56 (8 x 8 mm) Also supported TMC5130: the same register set with integrated MOSFETs (up to 1.4 A), detected at start-up TMC5160 datasheet · TMC5130 differences What you get ¶ One object per chip. TMC51x0<YourPort> exposes the chip as named subsystems: rampControl , motorControl , stallGuard , encoder , homing , status and more. See API guide . Current from the motor datasheet. Give rated current, sense resistor and supply; the driver computes GLOBAL_SCALER , IRUN and IHOLD . See Current and chopper . Physical units. Positions in degrees, steps or millimetres, speeds in RPM or rev/s, with lead screw, belt and gearbox ratios. See Motion and units . Sensorless homing. StallGuard2 threshold tuning and bounds finding without end switches. See StallGuard and homing . Several chips on one bus. SPI daisy chains and UART node addresses. See Multi-chip . Zero-overhead portability. The port is a CRTP class: no virtual calls, no RTOS dependency, every call returns Result<T> . See Porting . Tested without hardware. Host unit tests run the driver against a model of the chip's SPI interface. See Testing and CI . Where to go next ¶ Quickstart Wire the chip, write the port, turn the motor half a revolution. API guide ¶ How to do the common jobs with the driver: initialise, move, read, detect stalls, home, use an encoder and handle faults. Every snippet on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/api_tasks.cpp , with Driver standing for tmc51x0::TMC51x0<MySpi> and Unit for tmc51x0::Unit . The API reference lists every member. The shape of the API ¶ One TMC51x0<Comm> object per chip. Its public members are the chip's subsystems: Member Use it to rampControl Set the ramp mode, targets, speeds and accelerations; read position and speed motorControl Enable and disable the bridges, set currents, chopper, StealthChop, CoolStep, DcStep thresholds Set the speeds at which StealthChop, CoolStep and high-speed mode switch powerStage Set gate drive and short protection (TMC5160) switches , events Configure reference switches, latching, position compare; clear ramp events encoder Configure and read an ABN encoder, detect step loss stallGuard , tuning , homing Detect stalls, tune the threshold, find the ends of travel status , io Read faults, temperature, load, input pins, chip version communication , uartConfig Daisy-chain position, UART node address, clock printer Print decoded registers during bring-up Every call that touches the bus returns Result<T> . It converts to bool ( true = success), and has Value() , ValueOr(default) , Error() and ErrorMessage() : ErrorCode Meaning COMM_ERROR The port failed, a UART CRC was wrong, or a daisy-chain length was invalid NOT_INITIALIZED Called before Initialize() succeeded INVALID_VALUE A parameter is out of range (or a pin your port does not support) INVALID_STATE Not possible in the chip's mode, for example a ramp call with SD_MODE high TIMEOUT , CANCELLED A homing or tuning routine timed out or was cancelled HARDWARE_ERROR , SHORT_CIRCUIT , OPEN_LOAD , OVERTEMP_WARNING , OVERTEMP_SHUTDOWN A fault reported by the chip UNSUPPORTED The port or the chip variant does not have this feature Initialise ¶ tmc51x0 :: DriverConfig cfg {}; cfg . motor_spec . steps_per_rev = 200 ; // 1.8° motor cfg . motor_spec . rated_current_ma = 2000 ; // RMS, from the motor datasheet cfg . motor_spec . run_current_ma = 1500 ; // 0 = rated current cfg . motor_spec . hold_current_ma = 500 ; // 0 = 30 % of run current cfg . motor_spec . sense_resistor_mohm = 50 ; // 0.05 ohm cfg . motor_spec . supply_voltage_mv = 24000 ; cfg . chopper . mres = tmc51x0 :: MicrostepResolution :: MRES_256 ; auto r = driver . Initialize ( cfg , /*verbose=*/ false ); if ( ! r ) { std :: printf ( "init failed: %s 
 " , r . ErrorMessage ()); return false ; } return driver . motorControl . Enable (). IsOk (); Initialize() applies the whole DriverConfig : currents from motor_spec , power stage, chopper, StealthChop, global configuration, ramp defaults, reference switches and encoder. Pass verbose = false to skip the configuration table it logs. Configuration lists the fields. The destructor disables the bridges. Move to a position ¶ driver . rampControl . SetRampMode ( tmc51x0 :: RampMode :: POSITIONING ); driver . rampControl . SetMaxSpeed ( 120.0f , Unit :: RPM ); driver . rampControl . SetAccelerations ( 4.0f , 4.0f , Unit :: RevPerSec ); // accel, decel in rev/s² driver . rampControl . SetTargetPosition ( 90.0f , Unit :: Deg ); // absolute driver . rampControl . MoveRelative ( -45.0f , Unit :: Deg ); // from the current target driver . rampControl . SetTargetPosition ( 200.0f , Unit :: Steps ); // full steps: one turn of a 1.8° motor SetTargetPosition() starts the move as soon as XTARGET is written. MoveRelative() adds to the current target. Poll IsTargetReached() (or watch position_reached in SPI_STATUS ) for completion. Motion and units explains the ramp and the units. Run at a speed ¶ driver . rampControl . SetRampMode ( tmc51x0 :: RampMode :: VELOCITY_POS ); // or VELOCITY_NEG driver . rampControl . SetAcceleration ( 2.0f , Unit :: RevPerSec ); driver . rampControl . SetMaxSpeed ( 1.5f , Unit :: RevPerSec ); // runs until told otherwise driver . rampControl . Stop (); // decelerate to zero with AMAX In velocity mode the sign comes from the ramp mode, not from the speed. Stop() decelerates to zero. Read state ¶ auto pos = driver . rampControl . GetCurrentPosition ( Unit :: Deg ); // XACTUAL auto rpm = driver . rampControl . GetCurrentSpeed ( Unit :: RPM ); // VACTUAL auto [ err , standstill ] = driver . rampControl . IsStandstill (); // structured binding if ( pos && rpm && err == tmc51x0 :: ErrorCode :: OK ) { std :: printf ( "%.1f deg, %.1f rpm, %s 
 " , pos . Value (), rpm . Value (), standstill ? "stopped" : "moving" ); } const uint16_t load = driver . stallGuard . GetStallGuardResult (). ValueOr ( 0 ); // SG_RESULT, 0..1023 std :: printf ( "load %u 
 " , load ); Each read is one register access (two SPI datagrams). status has decoded readings: IsOvertempWarning() , IsStealthChopActive() , GetActualCurrentScale() , GetLostSteps() and more. Detect stalls ¶ driver . motorControl . SetStealthChopEnabled ( false ); // StallGuard2 needs SpreadCycle tmc51x0 :: StallGuardConfig sg {}; sg . threshold = 4 ; // SGT, -64..63: higher = less sensitive sg . enable_filter = true ; sg . min_velocity = 0.5f ; // TCOOLTHRS: ignore stalls below this speed sg . velocity_unit = Unit :: RevPerSec ; sg . stop_on_stall = true ; // sg_stop in SW_MODE if ( ! driver . stallGuard . ConfigureStallGuard ( sg )) { return false ; } return driver . stallGuard . IsStallDetected (). ValueOr ( false ); tmc51x0 :: StallGuardTuningResult result {}; auto r = driver . tuning . AutoTuneStallGuard ( 60.0f , result , // target speed, in RPM below -20 , 20 , // SGT search range 2.0f , // acceleration, rev/s² 30.0f , 90.0f , // speeds the SGT must also work at Unit :: RPM , Unit :: RevPerSec , 0.3f ); // 30 % current while tuning if ( r && result . tuning_success ) { tmc51x0 :: StallGuardConfig sg {}; sg . threshold = result . optimal_sgt ; driver . stallGuard . ConfigureStallGuard ( sg ); } StallGuard and homing explains the rules StallGuard2 needs and what the tuning does. Home the axis ¶ using Homing = Driver :: Homing ; Homing :: BoundsOptions opt {}; opt . speed_unit = Unit :: RPM ; opt . position_unit = Unit :: Deg ; opt . search_speed = 30.0f ; // RPM opt . search_span = 720.0f ; // at most two turns each way opt . backoff_distance = 5.0f ; // degrees off the hard stop opt . timeout_ms = 10000 ; Homing :: HomeConfig home {}; home . mode = Homing :: HomePlacement :: AtCenter ; // XACTUAL = 0 in the middle of the travel auto bounds = driver . homing . FindBounds ( Homing :: BoundsMethod :: StallGuard , opt , home ); if ( bounds && bounds . Value (). bounded ) { std :: printf ( "travel %.1f .. %.1f deg 
 " , bounds . Value (). min_bound , bounds . Value (). max_bound ); } Use an encoder ¶ tmc51x0 :: EncoderConfig enc {}; enc . pulses_per_rev = 4000 ; // counts per revolution after quadrature driver . encoder . Configure ( enc ); driver . encoder . SetResolution ( 200 , 4000 , false ); // motor full steps, encoder counts, inverted driver . encoder . SetAllowedDeviation ( 4 ); // full steps before deviation_warn auto x_enc = driver . encoder . GetPosition (); // X_ENC if ( driver . encoder . IsDeviationWarning (). ValueOr ( false )) { std :: printf ( "step loss: encoder at %ld 
 " , static_cast < long > ( x_enc . ValueOr ( 0 ))); driver . encoder . ClearDeviationWarning (); } SetResolution() writes ENC_CONST so X_ENC counts in the same microsteps as XACTUAL ; it uses a binary prescaler when the ratio is exact and a decimal one otherwise. SetAllowedDeviation() takes full steps and arms deviation_warn in ENC_STATUS . Handle errors and faults ¶ bool drv_err = false ; bool uv_cp = false ; auto reset = driver . status . GetGlobalStatus ( drv_err , uv_cp ); // GSTAT: true = reset occurred if ( reset . IsOk () && ( reset . Value () || drv_err || uv_cp )) { bool overtemp = false , prewarning = false ; driver . status . GetTemperatureStatus ( overtemp , prewarning ); bool s2g_a = false , s2g_b = false ; driver . status . IsShortToGround ( s2g_a , s2g_b ); bool ola = false , olb = false ; driver . status . CheckOpenLoad ( ola , olb ); std :: printf ( "reset=%d drv_err=%d uv_cp=%d ot=%d otpw=%d s2g=%d/%d ol=%d/%d 
 " , reset . Value (), drv_err , uv_cp , overtemp , prewarning , s2g_a , s2g_b , ola , olb ); driver . status . ClearGlobalStatus (); // write 1 to clear, after the fix } Signal Meaning Where to look A call returns an error The port failed, a CRC was wrong, or the chip is in the wrong mode ErrorMessage() , your port's log GSTAT.reset The chip was reset (power-up, VS or VCC_IO undervoltage) Run Initialize() again GSTAT.drv_err Overtemperature or short circuit switched the bridges off DRV_STATUS : ot , s2ga / s2gb , s2vsa / s2vsb GSTAT.uv_cp Charge-pump undervoltage VS too low, or a charge-pump capacitor missing DRV_STATUS.otpw Overtemperature pre-warning Reduce current or improve cooling DRV_STATUS.ola / olb Open load Motor wiring GSTAT is write-1-to-clear: clear it after you fixed the cause. A short-circuit shutdown stays latched until the driver is disabled, by DRV_ENN ( motorControl.Disable() ) or by TOFF = 0. After an overtemperature shutdown the bridges stay off until the chip has cooled below the pre-warning threshold. The open-load flags are informative only and can trigger falsely in fast motion and at standstill: check them during slow motion. Access a register directly ¶ auto & comm = driver . GetComm (); const uint8_t where = driver . communication . GetDaisyChainPosition (); // SPI: chain position auto drv_status = comm . ReadRegister ( tmc51x0 :: Registers :: DRV_STATUS , where ); if ( drv_status ) { std :: printf ( "DRV_STATUS = 0x%08lX 
 " , static_cast < unsigned long > ( drv_status . Value ())); } comm . WriteRegister ( tmc51x0 :: Registers :: TPOWERDOWN , 10 , where ); // write-only register Communication protocols has the register map.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is put together: three layers, what each owns, and how one call reaches the chip. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one TMC51x0 object per chip, whose public members are the chip's subsystems (listed from inc/tmc51x0.hpp). Each subsystem turns a call in physical units into register reads and writes. The communication interface (SpiCommInterface or UartCommInterface in inc/tmc51x0_comm_interface.hpp) builds the 40-bit SPI datagrams or CRC-checked UART frames, handles daisy-chain padding and node addresses. The platform port is the only code you write: the methods the interface calls on it, read from the header. Below it is the TMC5160 or TMC5130. Drawn from: inc/tmc51x0.hpp TMC51x0 members ; inc/tmc51x0_comm_interface.hpp SpiCommInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . docs.text: Current and chopper ¶ How the driver sets the coil current from the motor's datasheet, and how to choose between SpreadCycle, StealthChop, CoolStep and DcStep. Coil current ¶ Three settings multiply to the coil current: I RMS = ( GLOBAL_SCALER / 256) × ((CS + 1) / 32) × V FS / R SENSE / √2 with CS = IRUN while moving and IHOLD at standstill, and V FS = 325 mV typical. GLOBAL_SCALER is 32 to 255 (0 means 256; 1 to 31 are not allowed), IRUN and IHOLD are 0 to 31. You do not compute these. Fill DriverConfig::motor_spec and Initialize() (or motorControl.ConfigureMotorCurrent() ) does it: MotorSpec field Meaning Default rated_current_ma Motor rated current, RMS 1500 run_current_ma Run current; 0 uses the rated current 0 hold_current_ma Standstill current; 0 uses 30 % of the run current 0 sense_resistor_mohm R SENSE on your board 50 supply_voltage_mv VS 24000 steps_per_rev Full steps per revolution 200 winding_resistance_mohm , winding_inductance_mh Used for the StealthChop limits 3, 0 iholddelay_ms Time to ramp from run to hold current at standstill 100 scaler_adjustment_percent , irun_adjustment_percent , ihold_adjustment_percent Trim the calculated values 0 The calculation starts at IRUN = 31 and solves for GLOBAL_SCALER ; when the scaler would exceed 200 it lowers IRUN (not below 16) to keep the scaler in range. A run current more than 10 % above the full-scale current of the sense resistor fails. With 50 mΩ and 1500 mA the result is IRUN = 31, GLOBAL_SCALER ≈ 84 (derived). LogDerivedInitSummary() prints what was written; motorControl.SetCurrent(irun, ihold) and SetGlobalScaler() set the registers directly. TMC5130 The TMC5130 has no GLOBAL_SCALER , so the driver skips it, but the IRUN it calculates still assumes the scaler. Set the TMC5130's currents with SetCurrent() ( TMC5130 ). Choosing a chopper ¶ Mode What it does Choose it for Limits StealthChop2 Voltage-mode PWM, near silent Low and medium speed, standstill No StallGuard2; the first motion after power-up calibrates it ( IRUN ≥ 8) SpreadCycle Cycle-by-cycle current control High speed, high dynamics, any load Audible chopper noise at low speed CoolStep Lowers the current while StallGuard2 reports a light load Saving energy and heat Needs SpreadCycle above TCOOLTHRS DcStep Lets the motor slow down under overload instead of losing steps Variable loads near the torque limit Above VDCMIN ; set it up with the datasheet DriverConfig::global_config.en_stealthchop_mode (on by default) selects StealthChop. The chip then switches by speed, measured as TSTEP (the time between microsteps): Threshold Register Above this speed StealthChop to SpreadCycle TPWMTHRS SpreadCycle CoolStep and StallGuard2 active TCOOLTHRS CoolStep and the stall output work High-speed mode THIGH Full step ( vhighfs ) or classic chopper ( vhighchm ) Set the three at once in physical units with thresholds.SetModeChangeSpeeds() , or one at a time with SetStealthChopVelocityThreshold() , SetTcoolthrs() and SetHighSpeedThreshold() . // Switch between StealthChop (quiet, low speed), SpreadCycle and full step by speed. driver . thresholds . SetModeChangeSpeeds ( 1.0f , 0.5f , 5.0f , Unit :: RevPerSec ); // TPWMTHRS, TCOOLTHRS, THIGH // CoolStep: lower the current while the load is light (needs SpreadCycle and TCOOLTHRS). tmc51x0 :: CoolStepConfig cool {}; cool . lower_threshold_sg = 100 ; cool . upper_threshold_sg = 300 ; cool . min_velocity = 0.5f ; cool . velocity_unit = Unit :: RevPerSec ; driver . motorControl . ConfigureCoolStep ( cool ); // Change the run and hold currents (IRUN, IHOLD: 0..31 of the GLOBAL_SCALER full scale). driver . motorControl . SetCurrent ( 20 , 8 ); SpreadCycle timing ¶ ChopperConfig holds the CHOPCONF fields. The driver's defaults ( TOFF = 5, TBL = 2, HSTRT = 4, HEND = 0) work for most motors; tune HSTRT and HEND with the datasheet's procedure (chapter 7) when the motor is noisy or the current waveform is distorted. mres sets the microstep resolution (256 down to full step) and intpol interpolates lower resolutions to 256 microsteps. StealthChop PWM frequency ¶ StealthChopConfig::pwm_freq selects f PWM as a fraction of f CLK : pwm_freq f PWM At 12 MHz 0 2/1024 f CLK 23.4 kHz 1 (default) 2/683 f CLK 35.1 kHz 2 2/512 f CLK 46.9 kHz 3 2/410 f CLK 58.5 kHz Automatic tuning ( pwm_autoscale , pwm_autograd ) needs a run current of IRUN ≥ 8 and a first move at moderate speed. Changing GLOBAL_SCALER or VS afterwards invalidates the tuning until the chip re-tunes. Power stage (TMC5160) ¶ The TMC5160 drives external MOSFETs. docs.text: Three settings multiply to the coil current: I RMS = ( GLOBAL_SCALER / 256) × ((CS + 1) / 32) × V FS / R SENSE / √2 with CS = IRUN while moving and IHOLD at standstill, and V FS = 325 mV typical. GLOBAL_SCALER is 32 to 255 (0 means 256; 1 to 31 are not allowed), IRUN and IHOLD are 0 to 31. You do not compute these. Fill DriverConfig::motor_spec and Initialize() (or motorControl.ConfigureMotorCurrent() ) does it: MotorSpec field Meaning Default rated_current_ma Motor rated current, RMS 1500 run_current_ma Run current; 0 uses the rated current 0 hold_current_ma Standstill current; 0 uses 30 % of the run current 0 sense_resistor_mohm R SENSE on your board 50 supply_voltage_mv VS 24000 steps_per_rev Full steps per revolution 200 winding_resistance_mohm , winding_inductance_mh Used for the StealthChop limits 3, 0 iholddelay_ms Time to ramp from run to hold current at standstill 100 scaler_adjustment_percent , irun_adjustment_percent , ihold_adjustment_percent Trim the calculated values 0 The calculation starts at IRUN = 31 and solves for GLOBAL_SCALER ; when the scaler would exceed 200 it lowers IRUN (not below 16) to keep the scaler in range. A run current more than 10 % above the full-scale current of the sense resistor fails. With 50 mΩ and 1500 mA the result is IRUN = 31, GLOBAL_SCALER ≈ 84 (derived). LogDerivedInitSummary() prints what was written; motorControl.SetCurrent(irun, ihold) and SetGlobalScaler() set the registers directly. TMC5130 The TMC5130 has no GLOBAL_SCALER , so the driver skips it, but the IRUN it calculates still assumes the scaler. Set the TMC5130's currents with SetCurrent() ( TMC5130 ).

docs.text: Mode What it does Choose it for Limits StealthChop2 Voltage-mode PWM, near silent Low and medium speed, standstill No StallGuard2; the first motion after power-up calibrates it ( IRUN ≥ 8) SpreadCycle Cycle-by-cycle current control High speed, high dynamics, any load Audible chopper noise at low speed CoolStep Lowers the current while StallGuard2 reports a light load Saving energy and heat Needs SpreadCycle above TCOOLTHRS DcStep Lets the motor slow down under overload instead of losing steps Variable loads near the torque limit Above VDCMIN ; set it up with the datasheet DriverConfig::global_config.en_stealthchop_mode (on by default) selects StealthChop. The chip then switches by speed, measured as TSTEP (the time between microsteps): Threshold Register Above this speed StealthChop to SpreadCycle TPWMTHRS SpreadCycle CoolStep and StallGuard2 active TCOOLTHRS CoolStep and the stall output work High-speed mode THIGH Full step ( vhighfs ) or classic chopper ( vhighchm ) Set the three at once in physical units with thresholds.SetModeChangeSpeeds() , or one at a time with SetStealthChopVelocityThreshold() , SetTcoolthrs() and SetHighSpeedThreshold() . // Switch between StealthChop (quiet, low speed), SpreadCycle and full step by speed. driver . thresholds . ConfigureCoolStep ( cool ); // Change the run and hold currents (IRUN, IHOLD: 0..31 of the GLOBAL_SCALER full scale). driver . motorControl . SetCurrent ( 20 , 8 );

docs.text: Hardware ¶ What to connect between your MCU and a TMC5160, with which bus settings and supplies, and the board-level traps to avoid. All values here come from the TMC5160 / TMC5160A datasheet (Rev. 1.18, 2023-03-01). Pin numbers are given for the eTQFP48 package, with the QFN56 number in brackets. The TMC5130 has the same digital interface; check its own datasheet for its pinout and supply range ( TMC5130 ). Mode straps ¶ SPI_MODE and SD_MODE select the interface and the motion source. Tie them to GND or VCC_IO. Treat them as straps: hard-wire them, or change them only while the chip is unpowered. SPI_MODE (22) SD_MODE (21) Mode Use with this driver high low SPI, internal ramp generator Yes: the full API high high SPI, external STEP/DIR Yes: configuration and diagnostics; motion calls return INVALID_STATE low low Single-wire UART, internal ramp generator Yes: the full API over UartCommInterface low high Standalone STEP/DIR, configured by the CFG pins No serial interface SPI_MODE has an internal pull-down: left open it selects UART or standalone mode, not SPI. The driver reads SD_MODE back from IOIN and refuses ramp, homing, tuning and encoder calls when the chip runs from STEP/DIR. SPI pins ¶ Signal TMC5160 pin Direction (chip) Notes CSN_CFG3 13 (14) in Active low; hold it low for the whole datagram SCK_CFG2 14 (15) in SDI_CFG1 15 (16) in MOSI SDO_CFG0 16 (17) out, tristate MISO; released while CSN is high, so the bus can be shared UART pins ¶ Signal TMC5160 pin Direction (chip) Notes DIAG1_SWP 27 (28) in / out Single-wire data. Join the MCU's TX and RX to it DIAG0_SWN 26 (27) in / out Inverted data for a differential (RS485-like) bus. In a 3.3 V single-wire design tie it to half the I/O voltage; with 5 V I/O it can stay open SDI_CFG1 (NAI) 15 (16) in Next-address input for sequential addressing ( Multi-chip ) SDO_CFG0 (NAO) 16 (17) out Next-address output to the following chip's NAI (high after reset) Control and status pins ¶ The driver addresses these by name ( tmc51x0::TMC51x0CtrlPin ) and by state ( GpioSignal::ACTIVE / INACTIVE ); your port turns a state into a level ( Porting ). Pin TMC5160 pin What it does Driver use DRV_ENN (in) 28 (29) High switches the power stage off (outputs floating) motorControl.Enable() / Disable() drive EN CLK (in) 12 (13) GND for the internal clock, or an external clock SetClkFreq() on your port (optional) REFL_STEP, REFR_DIR (in) 17 (18), 18 (19) Left / right reference switch, or STEP / DIR when SD_MODE is high switches , homing ENCA, ENCB, ENCN (in) 24, 23, 25 (24, 23, 26) ABN encoder (SD_MODE low), or DcStep pins encoder DIAG0, DIAG1 (out) 26 (27), 27 (28) Interrupt / stall / position-compare outputs in SPI mode Optional: read through GpioRead() ENCA and ENCB have internal pull-downs. With SD_MODE low, pull ENCN to GND or VCC_IO when no encoder is fitted. In open-drain mode the DIAG outputs need an external pull-up of 47 kΩ or less. Bus settings ¶ Setting SPI UART Mode / format Mode 3 (CPOL = 1, CPHA = 1), MSB first 8N1, single wire, half duplex Speed Up to 4 MHz on the internal clock; up to 8 MHz with a 16 MHz external clock 9000 baud minimum, up to f CLK /16 (750 kbaud at 12 MHz); the chip detects the baud rate from each frame Frame 40 bits: address byte (bit 7 = write) and 32 data bits Write: 8 bytes. Read: 4-byte request, 8-byte reply. Sync nibble and CRC8 Chip select Low for the whole datagram; high time t CSH > 2 t CLK + 10 ns n/a Reply The data of a read arrives with the next datagram After SENDDELAY bit times (default 8; at least 2 × 8 with several nodes) Timing filter SPI inputs and DRV_ENN ignore pulses shorter than 20 ns A pause of more than 63 bit times resets the frame The datasheet limits SCK to half the system clock and asks for a further 10 % margin on the internal oscillator, which gives the 4 MHz above. The ESP32 examples run SPI at 500 kHz. sequenceDiagram participant H as Host participant C as TMC5160 H->>C: 1: read XACTUAL C-->>H: status + old data (discarded) H->>C: 2: read XACTUAL C-->>H: status + XACTUAL H->>C: 3: write VMAX C-->>H: status + XACTUAL H->>C: 4: read VMAX C-->>H: status + VMAX written in 3 Every reply starts with SPI_STATUS : reset, driver error, StallGuard, standstill, velocity and position reached, and the two stop switches. Communication protocols covers the datagrams in detail. Power ¶ Supply Range Notes VS (motor bridges, charge pump) 10 V to 55 V Full specification. Down to 8 V with short-to-GND protection inactive. 60 V absolute maximum, including ringing VSA (5 V and 11.5 V regulators) 10 V to 50 V Normally tied to VS VCC_IO (digital I/O) 3.0 V to 5.25 V Your MCU's I/O voltage; sets the level of every digital pin VCC (digital core) 5 V From the chip's own 5VOUT through 2.2 Ω to 3.3 Ω Connect the MCU ground to the TMC5160 ground plane. Supply current with the driver disabled is 18 mA typical at 24 V and 12 MHz. The internal clock is factory-calibrated to 12 MHz ± 0.5 MHz at 50 °C; an external clock may run from 4 MHz to 18 MHz (10 MHz to 16 MHz recommended). Size the supply path for the motor, not the chip The bridge switches the full coil current from VS. Put low-ESR bulk capacitance close to the MOSFETs, keep the sense-resistor ground loop short, and keep the motor connected while VS is on: unplugging a running motor produces a voltage spike that can exceed the 60 V rating. Sense resistor and current range ¶ Two sense resistors set the coil current range. The full-scale RMS current is I RMS,max = V FS / R SENSE / √2, with V FS = 325 mV typical, so 50 mΩ gives about 4.6 A RMS and 33 mΩ about 7.0 A RMS (derived from the formula, not measured). The driver scales the current down from there with GLOBAL_SCALER (32 to 256) and IRUN / IHOLD (0 to 31); give it sense_resistor_mohm and it does the arithmetic ( Current and chopper ). docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake or ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 12+ or a current MSVC. The CMake target requires cxx_std_20 . No RTOS and no exceptions: calls are noexcept and return Result<T> . The core allocates nothing on the heap; the string helpers that do ( GetDriverConfigString() ) disappear with TMC51X0_DISABLE_DEBUG_LOGGING . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to a version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-tmc5160-driver.git external/hf-tmc5160-driver git submodule update --init external/hf-tmc5160-driver Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples have their own submodules ( examples/esp32/scripts and two remote-controller projects); you do not need them to use the driver. CMake ¶ add_subdirectory ( external/hf-tmc5160-driver ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE hf_tmc51x0 ) # or the alias hf::tmc51x0 The hf_tmc51x0 target carries the include directories ( inc/ , inc/features/ , inc/registers/ , src/ and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect HF_TMC51X0_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on targets that link the driver HF_TMC51X0_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host unit tests in tests/ ( Testing and CI ) ESP-IDF ¶ The ESP-IDF component wrapper is examples/esp32/components/hf_tmc51x0/ . Copy that folder into your project's components/ (or point EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS at it) and set the HF_TMC51X0_ROOT cache variable to the driver checkout; the wrapper stops with a clear message when the path is wrong. Your component then declares REQUIRES hf_tmc51x0 . The wrapper depends on the IDF driver component. docs.text: Motion and units ¶ How the TMC5160's internal ramp generator moves the motor, and how the driver converts degrees, millimetres and RPM into register values. The ramp generator ¶ With SD_MODE low the chip generates the step pulses itself. You write a target and a speed profile; it accelerates, cruises and decelerates on its own, and the host only polls for completion. All motion parameters can be changed while the motor runs. Ramp mode RampMode Behaviour Positioning POSITIONING Moves to XTARGET with the full six-segment profile and stops there. Initialize() selects it Velocity, positive / negative VELOCITY_POS , VELOCITY_NEG Accelerates with AMAX to VMAX and keeps running Hold HOLD Keeps the current velocity unless a stop event occurs In positioning mode the chip uses a SixPoint ramp: Segment From → to Rate Driver call Start 0 → VSTART jump SetRampSpeeds() First acceleration VSTART → V1 A1 SetFirstAcceleration() Main acceleration V1 → VMAX AMAX SetAcceleration() , SetAccelerations() Main deceleration VMAX → V1 DMAX SetDeceleration() , SetAccelerations() Final deceleration V1 → VSTOP D1 SetFinalDeceleration() Stop VSTOP → 0 jump SetRampSpeeds() With V1 = 0 the ramp is a plain trapezoid using AMAX and DMAX . D1 must not be 0 in positioning mode, even when V1 is 0, and VSTOP must be at least VSTART . driver . rampControl . SetRampSpeeds ( 0.05f , 0.1f , 1.0f , Unit :: RevPerSec ); // VSTART, VSTOP, V1 driver . rampControl . SetFirstAcceleration ( 8.0f , Unit :: RevPerSec ); // A1: VSTART .. V1 driver . rampControl . SetAccelerations ( 4.0f , 4.0f , Unit :: RevPerSec ); // AMAX, DMAX: V1 .. VMAX driver . rampControl . SetFinalDeceleration ( 8.0f , Unit :: RevPerSec ); // D1: V1 .. VSTOP (never 0) driver . rampControl . SetMaxSpeed ( 3.0f , Unit :: RevPerSec ); // VMAX After a stop the chip waits TZEROWAIT before reversing ( SetZeroWaitTimeMs() ), and after TPOWERDOWN at standstill it lowers the current from IRUN to IHOLD ( SetPowerDownDelayMs() ). Units ¶ Every position, speed and acceleration call takes a Unit : Unit Position Speed Acceleration Steps full steps full steps/s full steps/s² Deg , Rad of the output shaft per second per second² RevPerSec n/a rev/s (the recommended default) rev/s² RPM n/a rev/min n/a Mm linear, needs a lead screw or belt mm/s mm/s² The register values are microsteps: one full step is 2 MRES microsteps (256 by default). The driver converts with the formulas of the datasheet (section 12.1): Quantity Register to physical Velocity v[µsteps/s] = VMAX × f CLK / 2 24 Acceleration a[µsteps/s²] = AMAX × f CLK ² / (512 × 256) / 2 24 Revolutions v[rev/s] = v[µsteps/s] / microsteps per full step / full steps per rev At the internal 12 MHz clock, 1 rev/s of a 200-step motor at 256 microsteps is 51 200 µsteps/s, a VMAX of about 71 600. The conversions use DriverConfig::external_clk_config.frequency_hz (0 means the internal 12 MHz), motor_spec.steps_per_rev and the current microstep resolution, so a change of MRES keeps the physical speed. The internal oscillator is accurate to about ± 4 %; feed an external clock where speed accuracy matters. Mechanical systems ¶ DriverConfig::mechanical turns motor revolutions into output motion. MechanicalSystemType Fields Effect DirectDrive none Degrees and revolutions are the motor shaft Gearbox gear_ratio (output / input) Degrees and revolutions are the output shaft LeadScrew lead_screw_pitch_mm Unit::Mm : one revolution = pitch BeltDrive belt_pulley_teeth , belt_pitch_mm Unit::Mm : one revolution = teeth × pitch // With cfg.mechanical = LeadScrew, 8 mm pitch, given to Initialize(): driver . rampControl . SetMaxSpeed ( 40.0f , Unit :: Mm ); // mm/s: 5 rev/s driver . rampControl . MoveRelative ( 12.5f , Unit :: Mm ); // 1.5625 rev const float where_mm = driver . rampControl . GetCurrentPosition ( Unit :: Mm ). ValueOr ( 0.0f ); std :: printf ( "at %.2f mm \n " , where_mm ); Millimetres need a mechanical system With DirectDrive or Gearbox , or a zero pitch, the Unit::Mm conversions return 0: a SetTargetPosition(x, Unit::Mm) then becomes a move to position 0. Configure mechanical before you use millimetres. Position readback ¶ GetCurrentPosition() reads XACTUAL ; GetTargetPosition() reads XTARGET . SetCurrentPosition() redefines where you are without moving (for homing), and can update the encoder count with it. The raw microstep values are available from GetCurrentPositionMicrosteps() and GetTargetPositionMicrosteps() . Next: Current and chopper .

Multi-chip ¶ How to drive several TMC5160s from one MCU: an SPI daisy chain on one chip select, or several nodes on one single-wire UART. Each chip gets its own TMC51x0 object; all of them share one port object. The driver passes each chip's position (SPI) or node address (UART) with every register access. SPI daisy chain ¶ The chips share CSN, SCK and MOSI. Data shifts through them: the MCU's MOSI feeds chip 0's SDI, each chip's SDO feeds the next chip's SDI, and the last chip's SDO returns to the MCU's MISO. flowchart TB MOSI[MCU MOSI] --> C0[Chip 0
SDI to SDO] C0 --> C1[Chip 1
SDI to SDO] C1 --> C2[Chip 2
SDI to SDO] C2 --> MISO[MCU MISO] Every chip has a 40-bit shift register. While CSN is low, bits clocked in on SDI come out on SDO 40 clocks later; when CSN rises, each chip takes the 40 bits it holds as its command. To reach chip k of n, the driver sends the command followed by padding, max(k + 1, n − k) × 5 bytes in one transfer, and takes chip k's reply from byte (n − k − 1) × 5. spi . SetDaisyChainLength ( 3 ); // three chips share CSN, SCK and MOSI tmc51x0 :: TMC51x0 < MySpi > x_axis ( spi , 0 ); // position 0: SDI on the MCU's MOSI tmc51x0 :: TMC51x0 < MySpi > y_axis ( spi , 1 ); tmc51x0 :: TMC51x0 < MySpi > z_axis ( spi , 2 ); // position 2: SDO on the MCU's MISO for ( auto * axis : { & x_axis , & y_axis , & z_axis }) { if ( ! axis -> Initialize ( cfg , false )) { std :: printf ( "chip %u did not initialise \n " , axis -> communication . GetDaisyChainPosition ()); } } Rule Detail Tell the interface the chain length SetDaisyChainLength(n) on the port before the first access. The interface also measures the chain on first use and logs a mismatch; it then uses the measured length Position 0 is next to MOSI The chip whose SDI is on the MCU's MOSI One transfer per access Your SpiTransfer() must keep CSN low for the whole buffer: 5 × n bytes or more Chain limit TMC51X0_SPI_MAX_CHAIN_DEVICES , 8 by default; raise it at compile time for longer chains Chips on separate chip selects are simpler: give each its own port object (or one port that selects the CS line) and leave the chain length at 1. UART nodes ¶ In UART mode (SPI_MODE and SD_MODE low) the chips share the single-wire bus and each answers to its own 8-bit node address. A chip's address is NODECONF.NODEADDR , plus one while its NAI pin is high. Wire NAI of the first chip to GND and each chip's NAO to the next chip's NAI. After power-up every NODEADDR is 0, so the first chip answers at 0 and all others at 1. Then, one chip at a time: Write the chip's final address into NODECONF through address 0. Drive its NAO low ( OUTPUT bit 0 = 0). The next chip's NAI goes low and it now answers at 0. Repeat for the next chip. // After power-up the first chip (NAI tied low) answers at address 0; the others answer at 1. tmc51x0 :: TMC51x0 < MyUart > first ( uart ); first . uartConfig . ConfigureUartNodeAddress ( 127 , 2 ); // NODECONF via address 0; SENDDELAY 2 for a shared bus first . io . SetSdoCfg0Polarity ( false ); // NAO low: the next chip now answers at 0 tmc51x0 :: TMC51x0 < MyUart > second ( uart ); second . uartConfig . ConfigureUartNodeAddress ( 126 , 2 ); second . io . SetSdoCfg0Polarity ( false ); for ( auto * node : { & first , & second }) { if ( ! node -> Initialize ( cfg , false )) { std :: printf ( "node %u did not initialise \n " , node -> communication . GetUartNodeAddress ()); } } Rule Detail Count addresses down Chips not yet programmed answer at 1, so give programmed chips high addresses, as the datasheet does (254, 253, ...) Addresses up to 127 with this driver The UART interface masks the node address to 7 bits on the wire, although NODEADDR holds 0 to 253 SENDDELAY of 2 or more With several nodes a shorter reply delay makes the other nodes see a transmission error Keep DriverConfig::uart_config at its defaults here A non-zero node_address or send_delay in it makes Initialize() write NODECONF again Power cycles reset NODECONF Program the addresses after every power-up For two chips, tying one NAI low and the other high gives addresses 0 and 1 without any programming. Helper classes inc/features/tmc51x0_daisy_chain.hpp ( TMC51x0DaisyChain ) and inc/features/tmc51x0_multi_node.hpp ( TMC51x0MultiNode ) wrap these procedures, but they do not compile today (among other errors, their constructors pass the wrong arguments to TMC51x0 ). Use the individual driver objects shown above. Next: Communication protocols .

docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the communication interface for SPI or UART. The driver never calls your SDK directly. It calls a few methods on a class you derive from tmc51x0::SpiCommInterface<Self> or tmc51x0::UartCommInterface<Self> (in inc/tmc51x0_comm_interface.hpp ). The base classes use CRTP: the calls are resolved at compile time, so there are no virtual functions and no vtable. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one TMC51x0 object per chip, whose public members are the chip's subsystems (listed from inc/tmc51x0.hpp). Each subsystem turns a call in physical units into register reads and writes. The communication interface (SpiCommInterface or UartCommInterface in inc/tmc51x0_comm_interface.hpp) builds the 40-bit SPI datagrams or CRC-checked UART frames, handles daisy-chain padding and node addresses. The platform port is the only code you write: the methods the interface calls on it, read from the header. Below it is the TMC5160 or TMC5130. Drawn from: inc/tmc51x0.hpp TMC51x0 members ; inc/tmc51x0_comm_interface.hpp SpiCommInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . What you implement ¶ Method SPI UART Contract GetMode() yes yes Return CommMode::SPI or CommMode::UART SpiTransfer(tx, rx, length) yes One full-duplex transfer of length bytes with CSN low throughout. length is a multiple of 5 UartSend(data, length) yes Send one frame (8 bytes for a write, 4 for a read request) and remove the echo UartReceive(data, length) yes Return success only when all length bytes (an 8-byte reply) arrived SetNaiPin(active) , GetNaoPin() yes Drive NAI / read NAO for sequential addressing; return UNSUPPORTED when not wired GpioSet(pin, signal) yes yes Drive a control pin (at least EN , DRV_ENN) to ACTIVE / INACTIVE GpioRead(pin) yes yes Read a pin as ACTIVE / INACTIVE ; return UNSUPPORTED / INVALID_VALUE for pins you do not have DelayMs(ms) , DelayUs(us) yes yes Block for at least that long DebugLog(level, tag, format, va_list) yes yes Print one line (0 = error ... 4 = verbose), or do nothing SetClkFreq(hz) optional optional Drive the CLK pin: 0 = tie low for the internal clock. Default: UNSUPPORTED SetPowerEnabled(on) optional optional Switch the chip's supply, for HardReset() by power cycle. Default: UNSUPPORTED All methods are noexcept and return tmc51x0::Result<...> where the table shows a result. SPI port ¶ my_spi.hpp class MySpi : public tmc51x0 :: SpiCommInterface < MySpi > { public : tmc51x0 :: CommMode GetMode () const noexcept { return tmc51x0 :: CommMode :: SPI ; } // One full-duplex transfer of `length` bytes (5 per chip in the chain), SPI mode 3, CSN low throughout. tmc51x0 :: Result < void > SpiTransfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , size_t length ) noexcept { if ( ! platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , length )) { return tmc51x0 :: Result < void > ( tmc51x0 :: ErrorCode :: COMM_ERROR ); } return tmc51x0 :: Result < void > (); } // ACTIVE / INACTIVE to a GPIO level. DRV_ENN is active low: ACTIVE (enabled) drives it low. tmc51x0 :: Result < void > GpioSet ( tmc51x0 :: TMC51x0CtrlPin pin , tmc51x0 :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { const int gpio = GpioOf ( pin ); const bool level = ( signal == tmc51x0 :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE ) == levels_ . GetActiveLevel ( pin ); if ( gpio < 0 || ! platform_gpio_write ( gpio , level )) { return tmc51x0 :: Result < void > ( tmc51x0 :: ErrorCode :: INVALID_VALUE ); } return tmc51x0 :: Result < void > (); } tmc51x0 :: Result < tmc51x0 :: GpioSignal > GpioRead ( tmc51x0 :: TMC51x0CtrlPin pin ) noexcept { bool level = false ; const int gpio = GpioOf ( pin ); if ( gpio < 0 || ! platform_gpio_read ( gpio , level )) { return tmc51x0 :: Result < tmc51x0 :: GpioSignal > ( tmc51x0 :: ErrorCode :: INVALID_VALUE ); } return tmc51x0 :: Result < tmc51x0 :: GpioSignal > ( level == levels_ . GetActiveLevel ( pin ) ? tmc51x0 :: GpioSignal :: ACTIVE : tmc51x0 :: GpioSignal :: INACTIVE ); } void DelayMs ( uint32_t ms ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( ms * 1000U ); } void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // Route driver logs to your logger (level 0 = error ... 4 = verbose), or leave it empty. void DebugLog ( int /*level*/ , const char * /*tag*/ , const char * /*format*/ , va_list /*args*/ ) noexcept {} private : static int GpioOf ( tmc51x0 :: TMC51x0CtrlPin pin ) noexcept { switch ( pin ) { case tmc51x0 :: TMC51x0CtrlPin :: EN : return 6 ; // DRV_ENN case tmc51x0 :: TMC51x0CtrlPin :: DIAG0 : return 7 ; // optional: interrupt / stall output case tmc51x0 :: TMC51x0CtrlPin :: DIAG1 : return 8 ; // optional: position compare output default : return -1 ; // not wired on this board } } tmc51x0 :: PinActiveLevels levels_ {}; // defaults: DRV_ENN active low, the other pins active high }; Rules the transfer must follow: SPI mode 3 , MSB first, up to 4 MHz on the chip's internal clock (8 MHz with a 16 MHz external clock). docs.text: Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the communication interface for SPI or UART. The driver never calls your SDK directly. It calls a few methods on a class you derive from tmc51x0::SpiCommInterface<Self> or tmc51x0::UartCommInterface<Self> (in inc/tmc51x0_comm_interface.hpp ). The base classes use CRTP: the calls are resolved at compile time, so there are no virtual functions and no vtable. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one TMC51x0 object per chip, whose public members are the chip's subsystems (listed from inc/tmc51x0.hpp). The platform port is the only code you write: the methods the interface calls on it, read from the header. Below it is the TMC5160 or TMC5130. docs.text: Communication protocols ¶ What goes over the wire: the SPI datagram, the UART frames, and how the driver uses them to read and write registers. You need this page to write a port, to read a logic-analyser trace or to access a register the API does not cover. The interface classes in inc/tmc51x0_comm_interface.hpp implement everything here. SPI datagram ¶ Each access is 40 bits, MSB first, with CSN low for the whole datagram: Bits Host to chip Chip to host 39 W: 1 = write, 0 = read SPI_STATUS bit 7 38..32 Register address SPI_STATUS bits 6..0 31..0 Data (zero for a read) Data latched by the previous datagram So a write of VMAX (0x27) = 0x00ABCDEF is the bytes A7 00 AB CD EF , and a read of XACTUAL (0x21) is 21 00 00 00 00 . The data of a read comes back with the next datagram, so the driver sends the read twice and takes the value from the second reply. After a write it sends a read of the same address and checks the reply, which carries the value just written. Each register access therefore costs two datagrams. SPI_STATUS ¶ The first byte of every SPI reply: Bit Name Meaning 7 status_stop_r Right stop switch active ( RAMP_STAT[1] ) 6 status_stop_l Left stop switch active ( RAMP_STAT[0] ) 5 position_reached Target position reached ( RAMP_STAT[9] ) 4 velocity_reached Target velocity reached ( RAMP_STAT[8] ) 3 standstill Motor at standstill ( DRV_STATUS[31] ) 2 sg2 StallGuard2 flag ( DRV_STATUS[24] ) 1 driver_error Driver error; clear GSTAT ( GSTAT[1] ) 0 reset_flag The chip was reset; clear GSTAT ( GSTAT[0] ) tmc51x0::SpiStatus decodes it ( PositionReached() , DriverError() , ...). The driver logs driver_error (rate-limited) but does not fail the access because of it: read GSTAT and DRV_STATUS to find the cause. UART frames ¶ Every byte is 8N1, LSB first; multi-byte data is sent high byte first. Each frame starts with the sync nibble ( 0x05 in the first byte) and ends with a CRC8. Frame Bytes Layout Write 8 05 , node address, register address | 0x80, 4 data bytes, CRC Read request 4 05 , node address, register address, CRC Read reply 8 05 , FF (master address), register address, 4 data bytes, CRC The CRC is CRC8 with polynomial x⁸ + x² + x + 1 over all preceding bytes, each byte taken LSB first, as in the datasheet's reference code. A write gets no reply; the chip counts accepted writes in IFCNT . The driver checks the CRC of every reply and returns COMM_ERROR on a mismatch. On a single wire the MCU receives its own transmission. Your port must discard that echo, so UartReceive() returns only the chip's reply ( Porting ). Register map ¶ Range Group Examples 0x00 – 0x0F General configuration GCONF , GSTAT , IFCNT , NODECONF , IOIN / OUTPUT , DRV_CONF , GLOBAL_SCALER 0x10 – 0x15 Velocity-dependent control IHOLD_IRUN , TPOWERDOWN , TSTEP , TPWMTHRS , TCOOLTHRS , THIGH 0x20 – 0x2D Ramp generator RAMPMODE , XACTUAL , VACTUAL , VSTART , A1 , V1 , AMAX , VMAX , DMAX , D1 , VSTOP , XTARGET 0x33 – 0x36 Ramp generator features VDCMIN , SW_MODE , RAMP_STAT , XLATCH 0x38 – 0x3D Encoder ENCMODE , X_ENC , ENC_CONST , ENC_STATUS , ENC_LATCH , ENC_DEVIATION 0x60 – 0x73 Motor driver MSLUT0..7 , CHOPCONF , COOLCONF , DCCTRL , DRV_STATUS , PWMCONF , PWM_SCALE , LOST_STEPS Most registers are write-only; the driver keeps a copy of what it wrote. GSTAT , RAMP_STAT and ENC_STATUS are cleared by writing 1 to a bit. The addresses are constants in tmc51x0::Registers and the bit fields are unions such as CHOPCONF_Register in inc/registers/ . Raw register access ¶ auto & comm = driver . GetComm (); const uint8_t where = driver . communication . GetDaisyChainPosition (); // SPI: chain position auto drv_status = comm . ReadRegister ( tmc51x0 :: Registers :: DRV_STATUS , where ); if ( drv_status ) { std :: printf ( "DRV_STATUS = 0x%08lX \n " , static_cast < unsigned long > ( drv_status . Value ())); } comm . WriteRegister ( tmc51x0 :: Registers :: TPOWERDOWN , 10 , where ); // write-only register GetComm() returns your port; ReadRegister() and WriteRegister() take the chip's daisy-chain position (SPI) or node address (UART) as the last argument. Writing a register behind the driver's back makes its copy stale: prefer the subsystem calls for anything they cover. Next: TMC5130 .

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Turn a stepper motor half a revolution from your MCU: wire the SPI bus and DRV_ENN, write a small port class, call six driver functions. Before you power the motor Set the current-limit of your bench supply to about the motor's rated current and keep the shaft free to turn. Never connect or disconnect the motor while VS is on: the inductive kick can destroy the MOSFETs. 1. Wire it ¶ MCU TMC5160 Notes SPI SCK, MOSI, MISO, CS SCK_CFG2, SDI_CFG1, SDO_CFG0, CSN_CFG3 SPI mode 3; up to 4 MHz on the internal clock, start at 1 MHz GPIO out DRV_ENN High switches the power stage off; the driver drives it low in Enable() VCC_IO supply SPI_MODE Strap high: SPI interface GND SD_MODE Strap low: internal ramp generator GND CLK Internal 12 MHz clock (or feed an external clock) GND GND One ground for MCU, logic and motor supply VCC_IO is the MCU's I/O voltage (3.3 V or 5 V). Hardware has the full pin list, the UART wiring and the power ranges. 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and link the hf_tmc51x0 CMake target (or include inc/ and build with C++20). Installation covers CMake and ESP-IDF. git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-tmc5160-driver.git external/hf-tmc5160-driver 3. Write the port ¶ The port is the only platform code. It moves bytes over SPI, sets and reads control pins and waits. docs.text: StallGuard and homing ¶ How the TMC5160 measures motor load without a sensor, how to tune the stall threshold, and how the driver uses it to find the ends of travel and home the axis. StallGuard2 ¶ StallGuard2 compares the back-EMF to the commanded current. SG_RESULT in DRV_STATUS is 0 to 1023: high with a light load, falling as the load rises, and 0 (or close to it) at a stall. The chip raises the stall flag when the value reaches 0 for the current threshold SGT . Rule Why SpreadCycle only StallGuard2 does not work in StealthChop. Disable StealthChop, or move above TPWMTHRS Above TCOOLTHRS The stall output and stop-on-stall are only active above this speed; below it the value is unreliable Moderate speed At very low speed the back-EMF is too small; at very high speed the motor runs out of voltage A fixed current SG_RESULT depends on the current; tune at the current you home with SGT runs from -64 to 63. Higher values make detection less sensitive; start at 0 and raise it when stalls are reported without a load, lower it when real stalls are missed. The filter ( enable_filter , sfilt ) averages four full steps for a steadier value at a quarter of the update rate. driver . motorControl . SetStealthChopEnabled ( false ); // StallGuard2 needs SpreadCycle tmc51x0 :: StallGuardConfig sg {}; sg . threshold = 4 ; // SGT, -64..63: higher = less sensitive sg . enable_filter = true ; sg . min_velocity = 0.5f ; // TCOOLTHRS: ignore stalls below this speed sg . velocity_unit = Unit :: RevPerSec ; sg . stop_on_stall = true ; // sg_stop in SW_MODE if ( ! driver . stallGuard . ConfigureStallGuard ( sg )) { return false ; } return driver . stallGuard . IsStallDetected (). ValueOr ( false ); stallGuard.GetStallGuardResult() reads SG_RESULT ; IsStallDetected() reads the latched stall event and ClearStallFlag() clears it. With stop_on_stall the ramp generator stops the motor itself ( SW_MODE.sg_stop ). The datasheet forbids combining it with soft stop ( SetSoftStop(true) , deceleration on a switch event); the driver returns INVALID_STATE if you try. Tune the threshold ¶ The driver can search for SGT by running the motor at a target speed and testing thresholds: tmc51x0 :: StallGuardTuningResult result {}; auto r = driver . tuning . AutoTuneStallGuard ( 60.0f , result , // target speed, in RPM below -20 , 20 , // SGT search range 2.0f , // acceleration, rev/s² 30.0f , 90.0f , // speeds the SGT must also work at Unit :: RPM , Unit :: RevPerSec , 0.3f ); // 30 % current while tuning if ( r && result . tuning_success ) { tmc51x0 :: StallGuardConfig sg {}; sg . threshold = result . optimal_sgt ; driver . stallGuard . ConfigureStallGuard ( sg ); } Call What it does tuning.TuneStallGuard() Finds the best SGT at the target speed, then checks it at the minimum and maximum speeds you give tuning.AutoTuneStallGuard() The same with the motor current reduced (30 % by default) for the duration, which makes stalls easier to detect and gentler on the mechanics The result reports optimal_sgt , whether it was found ( tuning_success ) and, when the minimum or maximum speed does not work with it, the speeds that do. Run the tuning with the motor free to turn: it does not need a hard stop. The stallguard_tuning example runs it on hardware. Find bounds and home ¶ homing.FindBounds() drives towards both ends of travel, records where it stopped, backs off and places the home position: using Homing = Driver :: Homing ; Homing :: BoundsOptions opt {}; opt . speed_unit = Unit :: RPM ; opt . position_unit = Unit :: Deg ; opt . search_speed = 30.0f ; // RPM opt . search_span = 720.0f ; // at most two turns each way opt . backoff_distance = 5.0f ; // degrees off the hard stop opt . timeout_ms = 10000 ; Homing :: HomeConfig home {}; home . mode = Homing :: HomePlacement :: AtCenter ; // XACTUAL = 0 in the middle of the travel auto bounds = driver . homing . FindBounds ( Homing :: BoundsMethod :: StallGuard , opt , home ); if ( bounds && bounds . Value (). bounded ) { std :: printf ( "travel %.1f .. %.1f deg \n " , bounds . Value (). min_bound , bounds . Value (). max_bound ); } BoundsMethod Detects an end by Needs StallGuard A stall against a hard stop A tuned SGT ; the routine switches to SpreadCycle and reduces the current ( current_reduction_factor , 0.3 by default) Switch The left or right reference switch Switches on REFL / REFR, configured with switches Encoder The encoder no longer following the motor An ABN encoder configured with encoder HomePlacement Position 0 after homing None Unchanged AtMin , AtMax At the lower or upper end AtCenter In the middle of the travel AtOffsetFromMin offset (in offset_unit ) above the lower end BoundsOptions sets the units, search speed, the most distance to try in each direction ( search_span ), backoff_distance , a timeout per direction, and optional acceleration and StallGuard overrides. The routines save StealthChop, currents and StallGuard settings first and restore them afterwards. Every routine takes an optional cancel callback ( bool (*)() ), polled while the motor moves. To home in one direction only, use PerformSensorlessHoming() , PerformSwitchHoming() or PerformEncoderIndexHoming() ; each returns the final position in microsteps. Homing moves into hard stops Sensorless homing deliberately stalls the motor. Use a reduced current and a low search speed, and check that your mechanics take the impact. Set search_span so a missed stall cannot drive the axis far past its travel. Next: Multi-chip .

Host unit tests ¶ The tests build the real driver against a register-file model of one chip behind SpiCommInterface . docs.text: TMC5130 ¶ What changes when the driver talks to a TMC5130 instead of a TMC5160, and what to watch for. The TMC5130 is the TMC5160's sibling with integrated MOSFETs: the same motion controller, the same SPI and UART interfaces and, for the registers both have, the same register map. The TMC5160 datasheet describes it as the software-compatible part for designs up to 1.4 A of motor current. Detection ¶ Initialize() reads the version field of IOIN (bits 31..24) and stores it: Chip IOIN.VERSION Constant TMC5130 0x11 tmc51x0::ChipVersion::TMC5130 TMC5160 0x30 tmc51x0::ChipVersion::TMC5160 status.GetChipVersion() returns it afterwards. An unreadable version is treated as a TMC5160. What differs ¶ Feature TMC5160 TMC5130 What the driver does Power stage External MOSFETs, DRV_CONF , SHORT_CONF Integrated MOSFETs Writes the power-stage registers on both Current scaling GLOBAL_SCALER (0x0B) No GLOBAL_SCALER Skips GLOBAL_SCALER once the chip is detected as a TMC5130 Motor current 1 A to several 10 A, set by R SENSE Up to about 1.4 A Calculates IRUN / IHOLD as for the TMC5160 Supply, pinout This site's Hardware page TMC5130 datasheet n/a Everything else (ramps, units, StallGuard2, CoolStep, StealthChop, encoder, reference switches, daisy chains and UART nodes) works the same way. Set the TMC5130's currents yourself The automatic current calculation chooses IRUN for a GLOBAL_SCALER the TMC5130 does not have, so the coil current ends up higher than run_current_ma , by up to 256 / GLOBAL_SCALER . docs.text: What changes when the driver talks to a TMC5130 instead of a TMC5160, and what to watch for. The TMC5130 is the TMC5160's sibling with integrated MOSFETs: the same motion controller, the same SPI and UART interfaces and, for the registers both have, the same register map. The TMC5160 datasheet describes it as the software-compatible part for designs up to 1.4 A of motor current.

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms you may see while bringing up a TMC5160 or TMC5130, their causes and the fix for each. Start with the cheapest check: read the chip version with io.ReadIcVersion() . 0x30 (TMC5160) or 0x11 (TMC5130) proves the bus, the straps and the supplies at once. Then build with logging on (the default) and read what Initialize() and printer.PrintAll() report. docs.text: Figures ¶ Every figure on this site is drawn by a Python module from facts extracted from the code, so it is rebuilt, not redrawn, when the code changes. CI runs hardfoc-docs figures --check and fails when a committed figure no longer matches the code. Each figure below lists the files it is drawn from. Three layers, one of them yours ¶ Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one TMC51x0 object per chip, whose public members are the chip's subsystems (listed from inc/tmc51x0.hpp). Each subsystem turns a call in physical units into register reads and writes. The communication interface (SpiCommInterface or UartCommInterface in inc/tmc51x0_comm_interface.hpp) builds the 40-bit SPI datagrams or CRC-checked UART frames, handles daisy-chain padding and node addresses. The platform port is the only code you write: the methods the interface calls on it, read from the header. Below it is the TMC5160 or TMC5130.
